articles.title: Jay-Z is the perfect Super Bowl shill for a league of billionaires
articles.summary: The rapper lends the NFL a veneer of credibility but is unlikely to push back on the establishment figures who run the league. On Monday the NFL named Jay-Z as the headliner for this season’s Super Bowl half-time show.
body: Goodell’s wish makes total sense: Jay-Z is the perfect choice for the half-time show, and that’s not a compliment. The NFL wants a shill who can still pass for a rebel, and nobody in American music plays that part better than Jay-Z.

His bootstraps story mirrors the platitudes Americans have been told for decades – work hard and you’ll get what you deserve. On paper, he’s the perfect avatar for America’s polluted ideas of capitalism. But the country Jay-Z is rapping to is in terrible shape. How many of us can relate to his lyrics in 2026? Gas and grocery prices have rocketed. SNAP enrollment fell more than 13% in a year as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act tightened the rules. Only 63% of adults say they could cover a surprise $400 expense.
points: The rapper lends the NFL a veneer of credibility but is unlikely to push back on the establishment figures who run the league.

articles.title: Latte Lath: Carrick never screamed, he knew how to listen
articles.summary: For Emmanuel Latte Lath, the big moment came within three minutes of his Bundesliga debut for Union Berlin. At the age of 27, it was his first appearance in a major European league. And he scored. "It was like an explosion, the emotion that I had inside."
body: It was a simple header against Eintracht Frankfurt but for Latte Lath it was much more than that. It was the culmination of a journey that began in the Republic of Cote d'Ivoire before emigrating to Italy at eight years old. More recently, it was a career that had stalled.

His transfer from Middlesbrough to Major League Soccer club Atlanta last year was worth £22.5m and all the pressure that this brings. Asked about the big move by Sky Sports, Latte Lath says: "It was difficult because I came there with a lot of expectation."

He explains: "It became really, really difficult. I really felt it on my skin, on my journey, on my career." Eleven goals in 48 games was no disgrace. But everyone, himself included, hoped for much more. "I really wanted to show them why I arrived there. And it did not work."

There were memories that made him smile. He got to play against Lionel Messi, for example. "I was really like a kid when you see your hero. It was unbelievable. I will never forget it. I also touched him. I could touch Messi," he says, laughing at the thought.

At the age of 27, it was his first appearance in a major European league.

articles.title: Lise Klaveness: ‘Certainly there are people that can challenge Infantino’
articles.summary: Norwegian federation president distances self from Fifa presidency but believes governing body can be reformed. As the rain whips around Oslo’s government quarter, Lise Klaveness is shielding herself from the wind, trying to work out tactics.
body: The president of the Norwegian Football Federation wants to re-engage Fifa, and other governing bodies, on the topic of remedy. A slightly arcane aspect of human rights policy in normal times, the importance of remedy became very clear in the aftermath of the World Cup in Qatar, when the families of those injured or killed in the work that led up to the tournament were left without financial compensation after Fifa chose to direct a legacy fund elsewhere.

At Klaveness’s prompting, Fifa conducted a review into the process. The report ultimately found the organisation did have a responsibility to provide remedy, but Fifa chose not to redirect the money. Klaveness wants to focus minds on the topic once again and make sure new practices are in place for Euro 2028, co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland, as well as the World Cup of 2034 in Saudi Arabia where labour movement sources suggest there is currently little to no external scrutiny on worker’s conditions.

articles.title: Kurtley Beale earns shock recall to Wallabies squad five years after last Test
articles.summary: Veteran could add to 95 caps as he returns aged 37. Ramm and Thomas to also join Australia’s spring tour. Veteran playmaker Kurtley Beale has been summoned for the Wallabies’ spring tour of the UK in a massive development ahead of next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia.
body: Beale on Wednesday answered an SOS call from coach Les Kiss to join the squad for next month’s three Tests against England, Scotland and Wales before the inaugural Nations Championship finals in the UK from 21-23 November.
The 95-Test capped Beale will replace midfielder Hunter Paisami, who is unavailable for due to personal reasons, while James Ramm and Kalani Thomas were also named to join the touring group.

But the 37-year-old’s inclusion will be the major talking point as Kiss seemingly considers biting the bullet and ending Australia’s revolving door of flawed five-eighths by backing a proven No 10 to steer the wobbly ship ahead of next year’s global showpiece.

Kiss’s predecessors Joe Schmidt, Eddie Jones, Dave Rennie and Michael Cheika have used almost a dozen different playmakers since Bernard Foley guided the Wallabies – under Cheika – to the 2015 World Cup final in England.

articles.title: Kuyt named Fenerbahce interim boss before Liverpool tie
articles.summary: Former Netherlands forward Dirk Kuyt is appointed Fenerbahce’s interim coach a week before they face his former club Liverpool in the Champions League.
body: The 46-year-old is stepping up to the role after being the assistant of Ismail Kartal, who resigned as the Turkish club's manager following the side's 2-1 defeat by arch rivals Galatasaray on Monday.
Fenerbahce said, external Kuyt, who won the Turkish league title with the club as a player in 2013-14, would hold the post "until a new head coach is appointed".
Kuyt's first game will be a league match against Goztepe on Saturday before Fenerbahce host Liverpool in a Champions League group stage tie on Wednesday, 4 November (17:45 GMT).
The Dutchman spent six years with the Anfield side,, external winning the League Cup with the Reds in 2012 and scoring 71 goals for them in 285 appearances.

articles.title: Expectation vs reality: What if Man Utd have become a mid-table team?
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has been given a stay of execution by Manchester United after the club considered making a fourth managerial change in four years following their defeat by Bournemouth.
body: Carrick, the club's eighth permanent boss since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, came under major scrutiny after their poor start to the season continued with the 3-0 loss at Old Trafford.
But what if United aren't an elite team underperforming - what if they are in fact a mid-table team whose results have made them look better than they are in the post-Ferguson era?

United's managers have paid the price for the club's struggles over the course of the last decade, but research for Between the Lines shows they have mostly overperformed in terms of points won in the Premier League relative to 'expected' points.

United's total of 669 points is the fifth-highest in the Premier League in that timeframe. But the Sky Sports expected points model, which factors the quality of a team's scoring chances for and against by game, puts United on 613, meaning they have taken 56 points more than expected.

articles.title: Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league
articles.summary: Finlay O'Neill thought his sporting days were over when his dislocated a knee at the age of 16. Now he is preparing to play a part in England's bid to retain the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup.
body: "If you'd said to me when I was told I couldn't play rugby league again that it's going to be the best thing to ever happen to me, I'd have said 'you're lying'. But discovering wheelchair rugby league, which is even better, has been a blessing."
Rugby league has always been an important part of Finlay O'Neill's life. When he dislocated a knee while playing in a game at the age of 16, he put it down to the rigours of the sport.
The knee popped back into place but continued to cause issues, leaving the Halifax teenager struggling on the field and with increasing pain off it too.
After extensive medical tests, he was diagnosed with shallow kneecaps and hypermobility. His sporting hopes seemed to be over.

But discovering wheelchair rugby league, which is even better, has been a blessing."

articles.title: The two teenage darts superstars ready to challenge Littler
articles.summary: Two-time World Darts Champion Luke Littler is only 19 - but there are already two other teenage superstars hot on his heels and relishing a chance to beat him.
body: Two-time World Youth Championship winner Mitchell Lawrie, 15, and Jayden Walker, 14, will both compete against the World No 1 in Netflix's Beat Luke Littler event on Friday, where the winner will take home an eye-watering bounty of £501,000.

The youngsters are just two of 24 finalists who could face the reigning world champion: if one of the contestants beat Littler, the event will end and they will take home the prize, with Littler having to win 24 legs in a row to deny his opponents.
Both Lawrie and Walker have faced Littler before and are laser-focused on the task at hand, but there is little doubt that there will be plenty more to come from the pair.
"It's life-changing money so I'm looking forward to it," Lawrie told Sky Sports.

articles.title: Rising star Domingos hopes to mastermind England's World Cup retention
articles.summary: Just 18 months ago, Luis Domingos had not played Wheelchair Rugby League and now he heads to Australia with the hope of defending a world title with England.
body: Despite picking up the sport not too long ago, it is not the first time that Domingos has made his mark on the international stage. Domingos used to represent Portugal in wheelchair basketball and was professional in the sport.
However, to finish his studies at university, he left wheelchair basketball. Then he attended a wheelchair rugby league training session and the rest, they say, is history.

After an Ashes call-up, Domingos has continued his rapid ascent in the sport and now will represent England in the World Cup, achieving a dream that did not exist just two years ago. Domingos qualifies for England due to residency.
England's wheelchair rugby league team head down under looking to defend their title as the best in the world and they start with pool games against Wales, USA, and Ireland.

articles.title: Derek Jeter Warns Brewers That World Series Game 4 Loss Can't 'Deflate' Them
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers will have to wait for their World Series championship celebration. The Tampa Bay Rays beat the Brewers 4-3 in 12 innings on Tuesday night at Tropicana Field on Ben Williamson’s walk-off single, avoiding elimination and forcing a Game 5 on Wednesday.
body: Brewers manager Pat Murphy’s message to the Brewers after their heartbreaking Game 4 loss was simple: Tampa Bay will go into Game 5 feeling good, and they should too. Derek Jeter thinks Murphy is spot-on.
"He said it was going to be hard. He understands this," the five-time World Series champion said. "It's as good as Tampa feels right now coming into tomorrow, because they’re going to sleep well.

"If you’re the Brewers, you can’t allow this to deflate you, because if someone told you in spring training you’d be up three games to one in the World Series with your ace on the mound, the best pitcher in all of baseball on the mound, they would all take it."
Murphy credited Tampa Bay and said Milwaukee has to move on quickly.
